**EARTH JUKEBOX – Hear What Satellites See**

Earth Jukebox transforms NASA Earth science visualizations into interactive sound experiences, making environmental phenomena like ocean currents, forest fires, and atmospheric CO₂ easier to explore through audio.

The project features an interactive Ocean Sonification Laboratory with adjustable speed, temperature, and direction controls, alongside experimental video-based colour detection that maps RGB values to sound frequencies.

**My Role – Concept, Creative Direction & Web Development:** I developed the project concept, designed and built the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, integrated NASA visualizations, and implemented the interactive audio and colour-detection features.

Our goal is to make Earth science more accessible and immersive by allowing people to hear what satellites see.
details:
EARTH JUKEBOX – Hear What Satellites See

Project Overview

EARTH JUKEBOX is an interactive web application that transforms NASA Earth science visualizations into sound, allowing users to explore ocean currents, forest fires, and atmospheric carbon dioxide through an auditory experience.

How It Works

The Ocean Sonification Laboratory lets users adjust current speed, water temperature, and direction to influence generated sounds. It also features experimental video-based colour detection that extracts RGB values and maps colour balance to sound frequencies. Separate illustrative audio demonstrations are available for forest fires and CO₂.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes Earth science more engaging and accessible by offering an alternative way to experience scientific visualizations through sound, encouraging curiosity and environmental awareness.

Technology Used

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Web Audio API, Canvas API, NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, TextEdit, Chrome, and Python local server.

Creativity and Innovation

The project combines NASA visualizations, interactive audio, and video-based colour analysis to turn visual scientific information into an immersive auditory experience.

Factors Considered

Accessibility, simplicity, user interaction, scientific relevance, and accurate NASA source attribution. Experimental sonification features are clearly distinguished from calibrated scientific measurements.

Our Vision: To help people not only see what is happening on Earth, but experience it in a different way — by hearing what satellites see.
